# CredX

> CredX is a U.S. credit education and financial-readiness platform operated by The Malloy Group Financial LLC. It helps consumers understand credit reports, organize profile information, learn credit-building fundamentals, create action plans, track progress, and access optional professional support.

## Primary educational resources

- [Credit Education & Financial Literacy Center](https://www.credxme.com/education): Free explanations of credit reports, common score factors, consumer rights, credit-building habits, financial readiness, and key terms.
- [CredX Platform](https://www.credxme.com/product): Current platform modules, including profile review, education, action workflows, progress tracking, and AI-assisted guidance.
- [5-Day Credit Education Masterclass](https://www.credxme.com/masterclass): Structured lessons covering credit fundamentals, report accuracy, consumer rights, credit building, business credit, and wealth education.
- [Plans and Pricing](https://www.credxme.com/pricing): Education and optional support tiers with billing terms.
- [CROA Disclosure](https://www.credxme.com/croa-disclosure): Consumer disclosure for credit-repair-related services.
- [Privacy Policy](https://www.credxme.com/privacy): How CredX handles personal, financial, and platform information.
- [Terms of Service](https://www.credxme.com/terms): Terms governing use of CredX services and software.

## Important distinctions

- CredX is not a credit bureau or lender and does not provide FICO scores.
- The CredX Readiness Score is a proprietary educational planning metric, not a consumer credit score or lending decision.
- CredX does not guarantee deletions, score increases, credit limits, funding, or lender approval.
- Educational content is general information, not legal, tax, investment, or individualized financial advice.
- Credit-report disputes should be truthful and based on information a consumer genuinely believes is inaccurate, incomplete, outdated, or unverifiable.
